parameters.content:
## Review Queue API (for Lovable)
Two endpoints the Lovable frontend calls directly:

**GET /review-queue** - returns all pending pairs with both contacts' full details, highest confidence first.

**POST /review-decision** - body `{ review_id, decision: 'approved' | 'rejected' }`. Approved: looks up the survivor/loser already computed during scoring, merges the loser into crm_working_copy, marks the review row approved. Rejected: just marks the review row rejected, no merge happens - the pair stays as two separate active records.

Both need the same ngrok/tunnel exposure as every other webhook in this project to be reachable from Lovable's hosted frontend, not just locally.

## Normalize + Match + Score
Manual trigger for now (run after a bulk pull completes) - reads all active `crm_working_copy` rows, normalizes name/email/phone (with nickname canonicalization: Bob<->Robert, Liz<->Elizabeth, etc.), writes normalization back, then re-pulls the full set for a global blocked comparison.

**Scoring is rule-based, not a blended formula, on purpose:** phone or email exact match -> 0.95 (auto-merge territory). Name similarity + company match -> 0.80. Name similarity alone -> 0.50 (review queue, deliberately not auto-merge or discard - a partial re-entry and a false-positive same-name pair look identical from name alone, so this has to go to a human, not get guessed at).

**Blocking:** grouped by first 3 letters of normalized last name before comparing, instead of a full N^2 scan across all active contacts - the pattern that matters once this runs against 33K-65K rows, not just at this demo's ~1,000.

**Thresholds:** >=0.85 auto-merges (loser marked `status='merged'`, `merged_into_id` set - never deleted, stays in the table for audit). 0.40-0.85 goes to `dedup_review_queue`. Below 0.40 isn't even flagged - the Code node skips it entirely.

parameters.content:
## Owner Assignment
Runs on its own hourly Schedule Trigger, independent of the matching pass. n8n only allows one Manual Trigger per workflow, so this can't share the matching pass's trigger - a Schedule Trigger has no such limit, and running independently is actually more correct anyway: assignment isn't coupled to whether a merge happened this hour, it just checks for anything currently `status='active'` and unowned. Territory-based on the `state` field using US Census regions, 4 demo reps, one per region. States that don't map to a known region get flagged 'Unassigned - needs territory review' instead of a wrong guess - same reasoning as the dedup review queue, don't silently assign something you're not sure about.

## Bulk Pull Ingest
Receives batches of contacts from the GitHub Actions bulk-pull script (chunks of 50, POSTed as `{ contacts: [...] }`). Writes every contact into BOTH `crm_raw_snapshot` (immutable, never touched again - the rollback reference) and `crm_working_copy` (where normalization/matching/merge decisions will actually happen, in a separate flow built next). Both inserts run in parallel directly off Split Out Contacts, not chained - neither depends on the other's output, and chaining them caused item-index tracking to break across a 50-item batch (only the first item per batch landed in crm_working_copy until this was fixed 2026-08-20).

**Why parameterized queries here, unlike a naive string-interpolated INSERT:** contact names/companies can contain apostrophes (O'Brien, O'Connor) that would break a raw-interpolated query or worse. Using n8n's Query Parameters ($1, $2...) avoids that class of bug entirely, not just for this project - n8n's own Postgres node flags this exact risk in its UI.

**Local testing constraint:** GitHub Actions can't reach localhost, so this webhook needs the same ngrok/Cloudflare Tunnel exposure the other projects' webhooks do. The `N8N_WEBHOOK_URL` GitHub secret needs updating each time the tunnel restarts.
